doc.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

title: Playing the Iridium
summary: The Nighthawks have succeeded at the modern-jazz Iridium, a rare good room after thirty years of hard clubs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Would a place like the Blue Note ever book a band like The Nighthawks?

I’d like them to do that but we’ve succeeded at Iridium, which was known for more modern jazz. We’d been doing some kind of irregular things at the Iridium if you want to say that, and it’s been very rewarding to play in a nice place like that with an actual fantastic Steinway piano that works, and music stands and lights that are already there and that wonderful sound system and a fellow on the sound board. To me this is a rarity these days for what I’ve been through and my little hardships of putting the band in clubs around New York in the last 30 years.
